fatal_errors: The proposed sluggish-diffusion stabilization mechanism is opposite to the observed active diffusion, surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, melting, and evaporation.
The prediction of retained phase and compositional uniformity conflicts with the observed instability above approximately 673 K and the 22% size reduction at 973 K.

Changing constituent elements to alter lattice distortion also changes surface energies, mixing enthalpies, crystal preferences, and evaporation behavior, so the controlled comparison cannot uniquely attribute stability to lattice distortion.
The cited evidence does not establish that lattice distortion suppresses diffusion in the proposed nanoparticles.
explanation: The response addresses the broad HEA-nanoparticle stability question and provides a testable comparison and falsification rule, but it does not reconstruct the target system or its governing mechanism. It omits the AuCoCuNiPt sub-10 nm particles, vacuum heating to 973 K, stepped in situ STEM-EDS analysis, morphology dependence, and atomistic diffusivity measurements. Most importantly, it advances entropy- and distortion-induced sluggish diffusion, whereas the target finds non-sluggish, kinetically controlled diffusion driven by surface-energy minimization, with Au/Cu surface segregation and eventual evaporation. E1 gives only general HEA entropy arguments and explicitly notes limits to entropy stabilization; E2 reports stability for another quinary system but does not support lattice-distortion-controlled diffusivity. Thus the alternative is conceivable in some HEAs but is inadequately evidenced and contradicted for the target material.
